alcance: Educational instructions for adults, adapted by the team. Terrestrial references: the mission's equipment and approved procedure take precedence. Pending review by flight medicine.

pulso.preparacion: If you want to log a resting pulse, rest for at least 10 minutes. Do not wait that long in an emergency.
pasos: Use the monitor according to its manual. As a manual alternative, place your index and middle fingers on the inside of the wrist, below the base of the thumb.
When you feel the beats, count them for one full minute.
Log the result in bpm and whether you were at rest or exercising.
pulso.errores: Comparing rest with exercise or losing count. If you cannot get a reading, do not make up a value or delay urgent help.
pulso.sin_equipo: You can count the pulse at the wrist if you know how. If you cannot find it, ask for support; this count does not replace assessing a person who is not responding.

presion_arterial.preparacion: For a routine measurement, empty your bladder and rest for 5 minutes. Avoid food and drink during the previous 30 minutes. Note it if these conditions were not met.
pasos: Use a properly sized cuff on the bare arm, following the blood pressure monitor's manual.
On Earth: back supported, legs uncrossed, feet flat and arm at chest height. In microgravity, use the restraint and position in the mission procedure.
Do not talk while it measures. Log systolic and diastolic in mmHg.
For a routine measurement, take at least two readings 1–2 minutes apart and keep each one.
presion_arterial.errores: A cuff over clothing, the wrong size, talking or comparing different positions can change the reading. Do not use the timing of a routine measurement to delay an emergency.
presion_arterial.sin_equipo: Without a blood pressure monitor you cannot get this value. Leave it unlogged and ask for the device; do not estimate it from the pulse.

oxigeno.preparacion: Read the pulse oximeter's manual. Keep your hand warm and relaxed; remove nail polish from the finger you use.
pasos: Place the pulse oximeter on the finger according to its manual and stay still.
Wait for a stable reading and log the SpO₂ saturation in %, without confusing it with the pulse.
Note symptoms, date and reading conditions. A number that looks good does not rule out shortness of breath.
oxigeno.errores: Movement, a cold hand, circulation, nail polish and skin pigmentation can affect accuracy. The pulse oximeter does not measure CO₂ or the quality of the ship's air.
oxigeno.sin_equipo: Do not estimate a percentage from how the person looks. If there is difficulty breathing, ask for help without waiting for the pulse oximeter.

glucosa.preparacion: Use the glucose meter only if it is part of the mission plan and you are trained. Wash and dry your hands well; check the supplies and how they were stored.
pasos: Follow the manual for the glucose meter, strips and lancet and the mission's blood-handling procedure.
Read the device's unit: this form accepts mg/dL. Do not copy a value in mmol/L as if it were mg/dL.
Log whether you were fasting or had eaten, plus the date and symptoms.
Dispose of sharps according to the onboard procedure; do not share single-use supplies.
glucosa.errores: Dirty or wet hands, badly stored strips, dehydration, certain substances and environmental conditions can affect the result. Do not adjust medication based on this prototype's colors.
glucosa.sin_equipo: Without a glucose meter and proper supplies, leave the value missing. The historical OSD-575 tests do not replace a personal reading.

temperatura.preparacion: Use a digital thermometer according to its manual. For a routine oral reading, wait 20–30 minutes after eating, smoking or drinking something cold or hot.
pasos: Clean the device according to its manual and the mission procedure.
Use the method approved for that device. If oral, place the probe under the tongue and close your mouth until the device signals.
Log °C and write the method in the notes: oral, armpit, ear or forehead. Do not compare methods as if they were equivalent.
temperatura.errores: Recent food or drink, exercise and different methods can change the reading. Do not add or subtract an improvised correction between methods.
temperatura.sin_equipo: Touching the forehead does not give a temperature in °C. Leave the value missing and report the symptoms.

sueno.preparacion: Choose a consistent criterion: hours actually slept, not just time in bed. This is a team diary, not a validated clinical test.
pasos: Write down the estimated hours of sleep for the day and the matching date.
Say in the notes whether you included naps and whether it is an estimate or a device reading.
Use the same criterion every day. The comparison groups by UTC date and keeps the last reading of each day.
sueno.errores: Logging the same day twice does not add hours in the comparison. One short night does not prove the cause of a symptom.
sueno.sin_equipo: You can log an honest estimate. If you do not remember, leave the value missing; do not enter zero to mean unknown.

fuente.nombre: NASA HRP — risk context; diary method defined by the team

animo.preparacion: Voluntary self-report of your current state. Team scale, without clinical validation; it does not diagnose a disorder.
pasos: Choose how you feel: 1 very low, 2 low, 3 medium, 4 good, 5 very good.
Log the date and, if you want, a note about the context.
Compare only using the same meaning of the scale. If you need help, say so regardless of the number.
animo.errores: Do not treat a score as a diagnosis or assign it to another person without asking them. It is not a fitness-for-duty test.
animo.sin_equipo: No sensor needed. If you prefer not to answer, leave the value missing.

fuente.nombre: NASA HRP — behavioral context; scale defined by the team

estres.preparacion: Voluntary self-report of your current stress. Team scale, without clinical validation.
pasos: Choose your perceived stress: 1 very low, 2 low, 3 medium, 4 high, 5 very high.
Log the date and context if you want to share it.
Ask for support when you need it, even if the scale shows a low value.
estres.errores: This scale goes the opposite way from mood: a higher number means more stress. Do not use it to diagnose or penalize a crew member.
estres.sin_equipo: No sensor needed. If you prefer not to answer, leave the value missing.
